note: The domain-NEUTRAL upper lattice (a small core of HQDM, Matthew West). Domain models extend it as data by declaring their own types with `specializes`; the machinery infers the neutral category by climbing this lattice. Sales concepts (Sale, Ownership, Payment) are domain specializations, never core. Process PHASES are a domain lifecycle (sale: configure→fulfilment; admissions: apply→enrol) — they live in the top-level domain model / journey, NOT here.
note_stepKinds: The NEUTRAL vocabulary of journey process-step kinds — the machinery interprets these, never a domain word. A journey step declares its `kind`; the runner (journey-view.mjs) dispatches on it and the shape gate (journey-schema.mjs) validates against it. Extend by adding an entry here (data), never by hardcoding a kind list in code.

stepKinds.label: Capture
stepKinds.note: host a model's configurator; commit its inputs

stepKinds.label: Configure downstream
stepKinds.note: configure a downstream model's free inputs while an upstream binding stays authoritative

stepKinds.label: Ceremony
stepKinds.note: perform a declared L0 activity + record its outcome

stepKinds.label: Preview
stepKinds.note: show a downstream model's live figures (read-only)

note_relations: Only `specialization` is interpreted (the reader climbs it for isA/leafCategoryOf). The other HQDM relations (classification, part_of, participant_in, temporal_part_of…) are real ontology but NOT executed by this framework, so they are not carried as inert vocabulary — a coupled/relational framework would re-derive them where they'd actually be traversed.
note_renderHints: Presentational annotation on the neutral types (NOT the pure lattice): glyph + render family, plus author-facing plain-language `label`/`hint` and an `authorable` RANK. `authorable` (a sort number; absent = not offered) marks the categories a NEW configurator can be created as — surfaced by hqdm.authorCategoryChoices for the studio's 'What is it?' picker, so the type vocabulary stays DATA here, never hardcoded in the UI. Labels are generic ontological English, not domain words.

amount_of_money.label: Amount of money
amount_of_money.hint: A monetary sum — a price, fee or deposit

physical_quantity.label: Quantity or measure
physical_quantity.hint: A number with a unit — length, weight, a count

class_of_physical_object.label: Physical thing
class_of_physical_object.hint: A tangible item someone configures and takes ownership of

party.label: Party
party.hint: An individual or organisation taking part
